mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has declined monotonically from -27.9% to -38.1% over four weeks, signaling sustained remote work adoption. This persistent workplace absence reduces commuting-adjacent retail visits, driving RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined every week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days exceeds RETAIL_REC mean over last 28 days, or WORKPLACES reverses to positive territory within 2 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility rebounded sharply from -15.9% to +11.0% week-on-week, indicating outdoor activity substitution for indoor retail. This behavioral shift toward parks crowds out retail-and-recreation visits, suppressing RETAIL_REC growth over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above 0% after two consecutive weeks below -10%
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumped from -15.9% to +11.0% in one week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases week-on-week in both of the next two weeks, or PARKS mobility falls below 0% again within 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has remained severely depressed (range -32.1% to -35.1%), constraining access to retail districts. When TRANSIT falls below -30%, reduced commuter throughput to retail zones directly suppresses RETAIL_REC. This mechanism persists as long as transit remains below -30%.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -30% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has not exceeded -32.1% in any of four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT rises above -25% and stays there for two weeks, yet RETAIL_REC does not increase, or RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days exceeds baseline.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC move in tandem because both depend on essential-trip consolidation behavior. When GROCERY_PHARM stabilizes near -6.6% (current level), consumers make fewer combined trips, and RETAIL_REC remains suppressed. The interaction of stable grocery demand with low retail demand creates a low-activity equilibrium.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains between -5% and -10% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC both negative across all four weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM rises above 0% while RETAIL_REC falls further, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 points while GROCERY_PHARM remains stable.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has increased from 6.0% to 7.7% and back to 7.0%, indicating sustained stay-at-home behavior. When RESIDENTIAL remains elevated above 6.5%, it signals policy or behavioral constraints on mobility that suppress all out-of-home activity including retail, driving RETAIL_REC lower over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 6.5% for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL has not fallen below 6.0% in any week
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL falls below 5.0% and RETAIL_REC does not increase within 2 weeks, or RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days exceeds last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT are jointly suppressed (both below -30%), indicating a coordinated collapse in commuting infrastructure use. This dual suppression creates a feedback loop: fewer workers commute, fewer transit riders, fewer retail visitors. The interaction of these two factors predicts sustained RETAIL_REC decline over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT fall below -30% simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES ranges -27.9% to -38.1%, TRANSIT ranges -32.1% to -35.1%
failure_condition: Either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT rises above -25% within 2 weeks, and RETAIL_REC increases by more than 3 points in the same period.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility swung from -15.9% to +11.0%, a 26.9-point reversal consistent with seasonal weather improvement. Seasonal outdoor activity expansion crowds out indoor retail. If PARKS remains above 5% for the next week, RETAIL_REC will decline as consumers substitute outdoor for indoor recreation.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above 5% in the current week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at +11.0% in t-0w, highest in snapshot
failure_condition: PARKS falls below 0% within one week, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 2 points in the next week despite PARKS remaining above 5%.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has stabilized at -24.7% after declining to -29.4%, suggesting a floor effect where the most mobility-sensitive consumers have already shifted behavior. GROCERY_PHARM stabilization at -6.6% indicates essential-trip consolidation is complete. The interaction of these two stabilizations predicts RETAIL_REC will remain flat or decline slightly, not recover, over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC week-on-week change is less than 3 points and GROCERY_PHARM is between -8% and -5%
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 4.7 points from t-1w to t-0w but remains -24.7%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 points in any single week over the next four weeks, or GROCERY_PHARM rises above 0% while RETAIL_REC remains flat.
